01 — Overview

THE BRIEF

Build a portfolio that feels as alive on a phone screen as it does on a cinema display — without compromising the atmosphere of the work.

Siva Kumar Murugan is a wildlife photographer and cinematographer whose work has appeared in National Geographic, BBC, and on Nikon's official pages. His portfolio needed to honour the cinematic weight of that work at every screen size — from a client viewing on a laptop to a potential collaborator scrolling on a phone at 2am.

The visual language was drawn from a viral Instagram reel — a video of fireflies flashing together in perfect synchrony in the Anamalai rainforest, shot by Siva over three nights. 902K likes. The palette it suggested — deep midnight blue-black, warm gold, parchment — became the spine of the entire design system.

The result is a fully responsive system with seven breakpoints, progressive disclosure of decorative elements, fluid typography, and touch-native interactions — all built to serve the work, not distract from it.

03 — Design Highlights

WHAT MAKES IT WORK

Four design decisions that give this portfolio its character at every screen size.

01
Progressive Disclosure
The film strip, side rail, ghost typography, and about-section illustration exist only on desktop — where the screen has space to breathe them in. As the viewport narrows, they step aside. The core hierarchy — name, work, contact — always stands alone, uncluttered.
Visual hierarchy
02
Fluid Typography via clamp()
Every heading uses CSS clamp() — minimum, preferred, and maximum values that scale continuously with the viewport. The Bebas Neue hero compresses from 9.5rem on cinema screens down to 3rem on phones, without a single hard break or orphaned word.
Responsive type
03
Touch-Native Overlays
On desktop, segment captions and image overlays appear only on hover — a deliberate choice that keeps the grid clean. On touch devices, a hover:none media query makes them permanently visible, ensuring mobile users always see what they're tapping into.
Touch interaction
04
Atmosphere at Every Scale
The firefly-inspired palette — void black, warm gold, parchment — was chosen because it reads as cinematic on a 27" monitor and as intimate on a 5" phone screen alike. The grain overlay, CSS scanlines on the hero, and radial gradients on segment cards survive every breakpoint without adjustment.

04 — Process

HOW WE BUILT IT

Every responsive system starts with a clear design language and ends with meticulous breakpoint testing.

01
Design Language First

Before any breakpoint was written, the full desktop experience was refined until it felt like the work itself — cinematic, deliberate, unhurried. The colour palette, typeface choices, and grid proportions were locked before responsive work began.

02
Desktop to Mobile

Responsive overrides were built in descending order — starting at 1024px and working down to 320px. At each step, the question was not "how do we fit this?" but "what should disappear so the rest can breathe?" Decorative elements were progressively hidden, never squeezed.

03
Touch & Accessibility

A hover:none layer handles touch devices. A prefers-reduced-motion layer respects vestibular needs. Tap targets are sized to WCAG AA minimum (44×44px). These aren't afterthoughts — they are part of the same design decision as the colour palette.

04
Tested & Verified

Each breakpoint was tested in Chrome DevTools, Safari mobile simulation, and on physical devices — iPhone SE (375px), iPad (768px), and 27" desktop. The grid, typography, and animation behaviour were confirmed consistent across all of them before delivery.
